note: Task areas for the turn writer. Written by hand from ordinary agent workloads, without reading any catalog skill's description. Each area gets 5 skill-seeking turns and 1 near-miss no-skill turn; 30 generic no-skill turns come on top (225 + 75 = 300).
setting: The user works with a general-purpose AI agent (in the style of Claude Code, Codex or OpenClaw) that can run shell commands, edit code, browse the web, call APIs and keep a personal knowledge base of notes about people, companies, meetings and ideas.

areas.scenario: Right after a meeting or call, the user wants what was said captured, and the people, companies and follow-ups in it connected to what they already know.
The user is about to meet or email someone and wants to know who they are and what has happened with them before.
The user is looking into a company (a startup, a vendor, a competitor) and wants a solid picture of it, drawing on both their own notes and the web.
The user found an article, paper, book, video or podcast and wants it saved, summarized and connected to their notes.
The user wants help organizing their day: their task list, priorities, what to prepare and what is overdue.
The user is behind on email and messages and wants to know who is waiting on them and what they promised.
The user has a large pile of old material (exports, folders of documents, old chat history, a drive dump) and wants it brought into their knowledge base.
The user has a claim, statistic or citation and wants to know whether it holds up and where it came from.
The user wants something written the way they write: a post, a reply, an essay, a newsletter.
The user's personal knowledge base needs care: installing it, upgrading it, fixing a broken sync or search, cleaning up messy pages.
The user wants to think through a topic or idea, pulling together everything they and others have written about it.
The user wants the agent to do something on a schedule or whenever some event happens, without being asked each time.
A code change is ready and the user wants it tested, versioned, described and put up for merge.
The user wants a careful review of a diff or branch before it merges.
The user wants their web app clicked through in a real browser to find what is broken.
Something is broken (a failing test, a crash, a production error) and the user wants the root cause found and fixed.
The user has an idea for a feature or product change and wants the plan pressure-tested before anyone builds it.
The user wants a screen, page or component to look better, or wants a design system or mockups made.
The user wants their code, dependencies or infrastructure checked for security problems.
Something is slow (a page, a query, a build, a service) and the user wants it measured and made faster.
The user wants documentation for their code: a README, API docs, architecture notes or release notes.
The user is building or fixing an iOS or Android app.
The user is building a web front end with a modern JavaScript framework.
The user is designing or building a backend service or API.
The user is working with a database: schema design, migrations, slow queries, a data fix.
The user is setting up or changing cloud infrastructure: containers, clusters, infrastructure as code, a cloud provider's services.
The user wants their build and deploy pipeline set up, fixed or sped up.
The user has a dataset and wants it cleaned, analyzed and charted.
The user wants to train, fine-tune or evaluate a machine learning model.
The user is a scientist (biology, chemistry, medicine, physics) who wants help with an analysis, a database lookup or a literature search in their field.
The user is building something on top of language models: an agent, a prompt, a retrieval pipeline, an eval.
The user needs help with version control: branches, a messy merge, history, a release tag.
The user wants tests written, fixed or made more reliable.
The user wants to extend their agent itself: write a new reusable procedure for it, connect a tool or server, tune its configuration.
The user leads a team and wants to look back at what shipped, how the week went, or how the team is working.
The user wants marketing work: landing page copy, search ranking, a launch, an email campaign.
The user wants help with social media: what to post, how to answer replies, how a post is doing.
The user is a founder thinking about strategy: what to build, pricing, fundraising, a board update.
The user is working deals: prospect lists, outreach, pipeline review, call prep.
The user has money or numbers work: a budget, a financial model, invoices, a spreadsheet to fix.
The user needs a contract, policy or compliance question handled.
The user needs a document produced or converted: a PDF, a slide deck, a word-processor file, a diagram.
The user is hiring or managing people: a job description, interview loop, performance review, onboarding.
The user handles customer issues: support tickets, a help center, user feedback themes.
The user wants a project organized: a roadmap, a spec, tickets, status reporting.

generic_no_skill: simple arithmetic or a unit conversion
a definition of a common word or concept
a yes/no clarification about something the agent just said
an opinion on a light everyday choice
a quick question about the current conversation
a one-line instruction to stop, wait or continue
